title.zh: 初中物理公式表与计算器

clips.send: Power from force and speed. Use the component of force along the motion. At a given instant use instantaneous speed. With a constant aligned force, average speed gives average power. This calculator uses a nonnegative force component along the motion.
clips.text: Power from force and speed. Use the component of force along the motion. At a given instant use instantaneous speed. With a constant aligned force, average speed gives average power. This calculator uses a nonnegative force component along the motion.

clips.send: Energy from meter readings. Subtract the earlier reading from the later one to get the energy used. Read any decimal digit shown on the meter.
clips.text: Energy from meter readings. Subtract the earlier reading from the later one to get the energy used. Read any decimal digit shown on the meter.

clips.send: Mechanical advantage. This is a force ratio. For an ideal machine it equals the input distance divided by the output distance.
clips.text: Mechanical advantage. This is a force ratio. For an ideal machine it equals the input distance divided by the output distance.

clips.send: Gravitational potential energy. Height is vertical and measured from the chosen zero level. This near-Earth model assumes uniform g and here uses heights at or above zero.
clips.text: Gravitational potential energy. Height is vertical and measured from the chosen zero level. This near-Earth model assumes uniform g and here uses heights at or above zero.

clips.send: Series resistance. Add resistances in the same path. Adding a positive series resistance increases the equivalent resistance.
clips.text: Series resistance. Add resistances in the same path. Adding a positive series resistance increases the equivalent resistance.

clips.send: Buoyancy from a spring scale. Rearrange to F浮 equals G minus T. Keep the object at rest and clear of the container. When measuring G in air, the model ignores air buoyancy.
clips.text: Buoyancy from a spring scale. Rearrange to F浮 = G − T. Keep the object at rest and clear of the container. When measuring G in air, the model ignores air buoyancy.

clips.send: Heat-engine efficiency. For a fuel-burning engine, the denominator is the energy released by the fuel. Use the same time interval for output and input.
clips.text: Heat-engine efficiency. For a fuel-burning engine, the denominator is the energy released by the fuel. Use the same time interval for output and input.

clips.send: Density. Pair the mass and volume of the same sample. 1 g/ cubic centimeters equals 1,000 kg/ cubic meters .
clips.text: Density. Pair the mass and volume of the same sample. 1 g/cm³ = 1,000 kg/m³.

clips.send: Latent heat. Use latent heat for the phase change itself, such as melting at the melting point. Calculate heating before or after it separately.
clips.text: Latent heat. Use latent heat for the phase change itself, such as melting at the melting point. Calculate heating before or after it separately.

clips.send: Fuel heat by volume. Use this form when q is given per cubic meter. Use the gas volume at the conditions specified for q.
clips.text: Fuel heat by volume. Use this form when q is given per cubic meter. Use the gas volume at the conditions specified for q.

clips.send: Total, useful and extra work. For lifting, useful work is Gh. Use the applied pull and the distance through which that pull acts to find total input work.
clips.text: Total, useful & extra work. For lifting, useful work is Gh. Use the applied pull and the distance through which that pull acts to find total input work.

clips.send: Pulley rope travel. The free end of an inextensible rope moves n times as far as the load in a vertical pulley setup.
clips.text: Pulley rope travel. The free end of an inextensible rope moves n times as far as the load in a vertical pulley setup.

clips.send: Liquid pressure. Measure depth vertically from the surface. This gives pressure due to the liquid alone, for a liquid at rest with uniform density.
clips.text: Liquid pressure. Measure depth vertically from the surface. This gives pressure due to the liquid alone, for a liquid at rest with uniform density.

clips.send: Joule heating. Square current and use constant current and resistance. For a purely resistive load, all electrical work becomes heat; a motor also transfers energy mechanically.
clips.text: Joule heating. Square current and use constant current and resistance. For a purely resistive load, all electrical work becomes heat; a motor also transfers energy mechanically.

clips.send: Fuel heat by mass. This is heat released by complete combustion. Only part of it may reach the object being heated.
clips.text: Fuel heat by mass. This is heat released by complete combustion. Only part of it may reach the object being heated.

clips.send: Parallel voltage. Both branches connect across the same two nodes. They have the same voltage as the parallel combination.
clips.text: Parallel voltage. Both branches connect across the same two nodes. They have the same voltage as the parallel combination.

clips.send: Average speed. Use total distance and total elapsed time, including stops. For steady motion this is also the constant speed.
clips.text: Average speed. Use total distance and total elapsed time, including stops. For steady motion this is also the constant speed.

clips.send: Wave speed. Wavelength is the distance between neighboring crests. In a fixed medium with a fixed wave speed, increasing frequency shortens the wavelength. For light in vacuum, v is about 3.0 times 10⁸ m/s.
clips.text: Wave speed. Wavelength is the distance between neighboring crests. In a fixed medium with a fixed wave speed, increasing frequency shortens the wavelength. For light in vacuum, v is about 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

clips.send: Electrical work from voltage and current. Use constant voltage and current. V times A times s gives joules. The billing unit is kWh, and 1 kWh equals 3.6 times 10⁶ J.
clips.text: Electrical work from voltage and current. Use constant voltage and current. V × A × s gives joules. The billing unit is kWh, and 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

clips.send: Plane mirror image size. The plane mirror image keeps the same size even when the object moves farther away. Its apparent size can change as you look from a different distance.
clips.text: Plane mirror image size. The plane mirror image keeps the same size even when the object moves farther away. Its apparent size can change as you look from a different distance.

clips.send: Average mechanical power. Power measures how fast work is done. Equal work done in less time requires greater average power.
clips.text: Average mechanical power. Power measures how fast work is done. Equal work done in less time requires greater average power.

clips.send: Series voltage. Add voltage drops in the same series path. They are equal only if the two resistances are equal at that current.
clips.text: Series voltage. Add voltage drops in the same series path. They are equal only if the two resistances are equal at that current.

clips.send: Parallel resistance. Add the reciprocals, then invert. With two positive finite resistors, the total is smaller than either resistor. For more branches, add more reciprocals.
clips.text: Parallel resistance. Add the reciprocals, then invert. With two positive finite resistors, the total is smaller than either resistor. For more branches, add more reciprocals.

clips.send: Total liquid pressure. For an open container, the surface pressure is atmospheric pressure. Under a sealed lid, use the pressure above the liquid.
clips.text: Total liquid pressure. For an open container, the surface pressure is atmospheric pressure. Under a sealed lid, use the pressure above the liquid.

clips.send: Ohm’s law. Use voltage, current and resistance for the same device under the same conditions. A filament lamp’s resistance changes as its temperature changes.
clips.text: Ohm’s law. Use voltage, current and resistance for the same device under the same conditions. A filament lamp’s resistance changes as its temperature changes.

clips.send: Voltage division in series. The same current flows through both resistors. For nonzero voltage drops, U1/U2 equals R1/R2. If both voltages are zero, the voltages alone give no resistance ratio.
clips.text: Voltage division in series. The same current flows through both resistors. For nonzero voltage drops, U₁/U₂ = R₁/R₂. If both voltages are zero, the voltages alone give no resistance ratio.

clips.send: Plane mirror distances. Measure each distance perpendicular to the mirror. The image is virtual and appears behind the mirror.
clips.text: Plane mirror distances. Measure each distance perpendicular to the mirror. The image is virtual and appears behind the mirror.

clips.send: Parallel current. The main current splits between the branches. Different branch resistances generally give different currents.
clips.text: Parallel current. The main current splits between the branches. Different branch resistances generally give different currents.

clips.send: Current division in parallel. Both resistors have the same voltage across them. For nonzero branch currents, I1/I2 equals R2/R1. If both currents are zero, the currents alone give no resistance ratio.
clips.text: Current division in parallel. Both resistors have the same voltage across them. For nonzero branch currents, I₁/I₂ = R₂/R₁. If both currents are zero, the currents alone give no resistance ratio.

clips.send: Current and charge. This gives the average current magnitude for steady flow in one direction. Charge q is measured in coulombs.
clips.text: Current and charge. This gives the average current magnitude for steady flow in one direction. Charge q is measured in coulombs.

clips.send: Convex lens, real image. This positive-distance form models a thin converging lens with a real image. The object must be farther from the lens than its focal length. At u equals 2f the image is real, inverted and the same size.
clips.text: Convex lens, real image. This positive-distance form models a thin converging lens with a real image. The object must be farther from the lens than its focal length. At u = 2f the image is real, inverted and the same size.

clips.send: Series current. There is only one path. The current has the same value before, between and after the components.
clips.text: Series current. There is only one path. The current has the same value before, between and after the components.

clips.send: Ideal pulley force. Count the rope segments supporting the moving block. Assume vertical segments, steady lift, and negligible friction, rope mass and moving-pulley weight.
clips.text: Ideal pulley force. Count the rope segments supporting the moving block. Assume vertical segments, steady lift, and negligible friction, rope mass and moving-pulley weight.

clips.send: Archimedes’ principle. In a liquid, buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced liquid. Use the liquid’s density and the submerged volume. For a partly submerged object, the displaced volume is smaller than the object volume.
clips.text: Archimedes’ principle. In a liquid, buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced liquid. Use the liquid’s density and the submerged volume. For a partly submerged object, the displaced volume is smaller than the object volume.

clips.send: Echo distance. Echo time covers a round trip along the same path. Use the sound speed for the medium and conditions in the problem.
clips.text: Echo distance. Echo time covers a round trip along the same path. Use the sound speed for the medium and conditions in the problem.

clips.send: Law of reflection. Measure both angles from the normal, the line perpendicular to the mirror surface.
clips.text: Law of reflection. Measure both angles from the normal, the line perpendicular to the mirror surface.

clips.send: Average acceleration. Choose a positive direction. Compute final velocity minus initial velocity along that axis.
clips.text: Average acceleration. Choose a positive direction. Compute final velocity minus initial velocity along that axis.

clips.send: Resistor power from current. At fixed current, a larger resistance dissipates more power. A change in resistance can also change the current.
clips.text: Resistor power from current. At fixed current, a larger resistance dissipates more power. A change in resistance can also change the current.

clips.send: Same distance, half the time. What happens to speed? Try it on the track, then review with formulas, units and worked problems.
clips.text: Same distance, half the time. What happens to speed? Try it on the track, then review with formulas, units and worked problems.

clips.send: Newton’s second law. Add the forces with signs along the chosen axis first. The acceleration follows the net force.
clips.text: Newton’s second law. Add the forces with signs along the chosen axis first. The acceleration follows the net force.

clips.send: Electric power. Use the device’s actual terminal voltage and current. Rated power applies at the rated operating conditions. Average power is W/t.
clips.text: Electric power. Use the device’s actual terminal voltage and current. Rated power applies at the rated operating conditions. Average power is W/t.

clips.send: Heat exchange. This two-body model assumes negligible heat transfer to the surroundings or container. Use positive magnitudes on both sides.
clips.text: Heat exchange. This two-body model assumes negligible heat transfer to the surroundings or container. Use positive magnitudes on both sides.

clips.send: Resistor power from voltage. At fixed voltage, a larger resistance dissipates less power. Use the voltage across that resistor.
clips.text: Resistor power from voltage. At fixed voltage, a larger resistance dissipates less power. Use the voltage across that resistor.

clips.send: Electrical energy from power. Use constant power or average power over the interval. Multiplying kW by h gives kWh, which is a unit of energy.
clips.text: Electrical energy from power. Use constant power or average power over the interval. Multiplying kW by h gives kWh, which is a unit of energy.

clips.send: Lever equilibrium. Each arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action. The two torques must act in opposite directions.
clips.text: Lever equilibrium. Each arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action. The two torques must act in opposite directions.

clips.send: Specific heat. Use the temperature difference. This form gives the magnitude of heat absorbed or released, with no phase change and approximately constant specific heat.
clips.text: Specific heat. Use the temperature difference. This form gives the magnitude of heat absorbed or released, with no phase change and approximately constant specific heat.

clips.send: Weight. Mass is measured in kg. Weight is a force measured in N and changes with location when g changes.
clips.text: Weight. Mass is measured in kg. Weight is a force measured in N and changes with location when g changes.

clips.send: Pulley force including pulley weight. Each vertical rope segment carries the same tension in this model. Count the moving assembly’s weight as well as the load. Assume a steady lift and negligible rope mass and friction.
clips.text: Pulley force including pulley weight. Each vertical rope segment carries the same tension in this model. Count the moving assembly’s weight as well as the load. Assume a steady lift and negligible rope mass and friction.

clips.send: Celsius and kelvin. Apply the offset to a temperature reading. For a change in temperature, an interval of 1 degrees Celsius equals 1 K.
clips.text: Celsius and kelvin. Apply the offset to a temperature reading. For a change in temperature, an interval of 1 °C equals 1 K.

clips.send: Kinetic energy. Square the speed before multiplying. At fixed mass, doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.
clips.text: Kinetic energy. Square the speed before multiplying. At fixed mass, doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.

clips.send: Two-force balance. The forces must act on the same object along the same line in opposite directions.
clips.text: Two-force balance. The forces must act on the same object along the same line in opposite directions.

clips.send: Volume by water displacement. Subtract the initial reading. The difference gives the whole object’s volume when it is fully submerged, with no overflow or trapped air.
clips.text: Volume by water displacement. Subtract the initial reading. The difference gives the whole object’s volume when it is fully submerged, with no overflow or trapped air.

clips.send: Floating or suspended at rest. Equality holds when buoyancy and weight are the only vertical forces and the object is in equilibrium. A rising or sinking object can have other force balances.
clips.text: Floating or suspended at rest. Equality holds when buoyancy and weight are the only vertical forces and the object is in equilibrium. A rising or sinking object can have other force balances.

clips.send: Mechanical energy. This model includes kinetic and gravitational potential energy. Add elastic potential energy too when a spring stores energy. With only gravity doing work, this sum stays constant.
clips.text: Mechanical energy. This model includes kinetic and gravitational potential energy. Add elastic potential energy too when a spring stores energy. With only gravity doing work, this sum stays constant.

clips.send: Energy from meter pulses. If the meter constant is given in pulses per kWh (imp/kWh) or turns per kWh (r/kWh), the quotient is in kWh. Count the pulses or complete turns during the interval.
clips.text: Energy from meter pulses. If the meter constant is given in pulses per kWh (imp/kWh) or turns per kWh (r/kWh), the quotient is in kWh. Count the pulses or complete turns during the interval.

clips.send: Mechanical work. This card assumes a constant force and motion in the same direction. A supporting force does no work on a motionless book.
clips.text: Mechanical work. This card assumes a constant force and motion in the same direction. A supporting force does no work on a motionless book.

clips.send: Period and frequency. Period is the time for one full cycle, and frequency is the number of cycles per second.
clips.text: Period and frequency. Period is the time for one full cycle, and frequency is the number of cycles per second.

clips.send: Contact pressure. Use the actual contact area and the perpendicular force. 1 square centimeters equals 0.0001 square meters .
clips.text: Contact pressure. Use the actual contact area and the perpendicular force. 1 cm² = 0.0001 m².

clips.send: Mechanical efficiency. Divide useful work by input work and express the ratio as a percentage. Useful work cannot exceed input work.
clips.text: Mechanical efficiency. Divide useful work by input work and express the ratio as a percentage. Useful work cannot exceed input work.

clips.send: 液体压强。深度从液面竖直向下量。液体静止且密度均匀时，本式求的是液体自身产生的压强。
clips.text: 液体压强。深度从液面竖直向下量。液体静止且密度均匀时，本式求的是液体自身产生的压强。

clips.send: 用电压和电流求电功。电压和电流应保持不变。V 乘 A 乘 s 得到 J。电费常用 kWh 计量，1 kWh等于3.6 乘 10⁶ J。
clips.text: 用电压和电流求电功。电压和电流应保持不变。V × A × s 得到 J。电费常用 kWh 计量，1 kWh＝3.6 × 10⁶ J。

clips.send: 阿基米德原理。浮力等于排开液体的重力。用液体密度和物体浸入液体部分的体积。物体部分浸入时，排开液体的体积小于物体总体积。
clips.text: 阿基米德原理。浮力等于排开液体的重力。用液体密度和物体浸入液体部分的体积。物体部分浸入时，排开液体的体积小于物体总体积。

clips.send: 比热容公式。用温度差。物态不变、比热容近似恒定时，本式给出吸热量或放热量的大小。
clips.text: 比热容公式。用温度差。物态不变、比热容近似恒定时，本式给出吸热量或放热量的大小。

clips.send: 平面镜成像的像距与物距。两段距离都沿垂直于镜面的方向测量。虚像看起来在镜后。
clips.text: 平面镜成像的像距与物距。两段距离都沿垂直于镜面的方向测量。虚像看起来在镜后。

clips.send: 漂浮或悬浮时的平衡。物体只受浮力和重力且处于平衡状态时，两力大小相等。上浮或下沉时要根据实际受力判断。
clips.text: 漂浮或悬浮时的平衡。物体只受浮力和重力且处于平衡状态时，两力大小相等。上浮或下沉时要根据实际受力判断。

clips.send: 串联电路的总电阻。同一串联通路中，各电阻直接相加。再串联一个电阻，总电阻会增大。
clips.text: 串联电路的总电阻。同一串联通路中，各电阻直接相加。再串联一个电阻，总电阻会增大。

clips.send: 波速。相邻两个波峰之间的距离就是波长。在同一介质中，若波速不变，频率越高，波长越短。光在真空中的速度约为 3.0 乘 10⁸ m/s。
clips.text: 波速。相邻两个波峰之间的距离就是波长。在同一介质中，若波速不变，频率越高，波长越短。光在真空中的速度约为 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s。

clips.send: 电流与电荷量。电荷单向流动时，本式可求平均电流的大小；电荷量 q 的单位是库仑。
clips.text: 电流与电荷量。电荷单向流动时，本式可求平均电流的大小；电荷量 q 的单位是库仑。

clips.send: 并联电路的电流。干路电流等于各支路电流之和。支路电阻不同时，支路电流通常也不同。
clips.text: 并联电路的电流。干路电流等于各支路电流之和。支路电阻不同时，支路电流通常也不同。

clips.send: 重力。质量的单位是 kg，重力的单位是 N。g 随地点变化时，重力也随之变化。
clips.text: 重力。质量的单位是 kg，重力的单位是 N。g 随地点变化时，重力也随之变化。

clips.send: 凸透镜成实像。此式取正距离，适用于薄凸透镜成实像，物距必须大于焦距。当 u等于2f 时，成倒立、等大的实像。
clips.text: 凸透镜成实像。此式取正距离，适用于薄凸透镜成实像，物距必须大于焦距。当 u＝2f 时，成倒立、等大的实像。

clips.send: 串联电路的分压规律。两个串联电阻中的电流相同。两电压均不为零时，U1/U2等于R1/R2。若两端电压都为零，仅凭电压无法确定电阻之比。
clips.text: 串联电路的分压规律。两个串联电阻中的电流相同。两电压均不为零时，U₁/U₂＝R₁/R₂。若两端电压都为零，仅凭电压无法确定电阻之比。

clips.send: 机械增益（力的倍率）。它是力的比值。对理想机械，它也等于输入端移动距离与输出端移动距离的比值。
clips.text: 机械增益（力的倍率）。它是力的比值。对理想机械，它也等于输入端移动距离与输出端移动距离的比值。

clips.send: 串联电路的电压。串联时总电压是各元件电压之和。同一电流下，两元件电阻相等时，分压才相等。
clips.text: 串联电路的电压。串联时总电压是各元件电压之和。同一电流下，两元件电阻相等时，分压才相等。

clips.send: 滑轮组的绳端移动距离。在竖直的滑轮组中，绳子不可伸长时，自由端移动距离是重物上升高度的 n 倍。
clips.text: 滑轮组的绳端移动距离。在竖直的滑轮组中，绳子不可伸长时，自由端移动距离是重物上升高度的 n 倍。

clips.send: 周期与频率。周期是完成一次全振动所用的时间；频率是每秒完成全振动的次数。
clips.text: 周期与频率。周期是完成一次全振动所用的时间；频率是每秒完成全振动的次数。

clips.send: 光的反射定律。入射角和反射角都以法线为基准，法线垂直于镜面。
clips.text: 光的反射定律。入射角和反射角都以法线为基准，法线垂直于镜面。

clips.send: 用电流求电阻功率。电流相同时，电阻越大，热功率越大。电阻变化也可能使电流发生变化。
clips.text: 用电流求电阻功率。电流相同时，电阻越大，热功率越大。电阻变化也可能使电流发生变化。

clips.send: 物态变化的潜热。潜热对应物态变化本身，例如在熔点熔化。物态变化前后的升温需另外计算。
clips.text: 物态变化的潜热。潜热对应物态变化本身，例如在熔点熔化。物态变化前后的升温需另外计算。

clips.send: 并联电路的分流规律。两个并联电阻两端的电压相同。两支路电流均不为零时，I1/I2等于R2/R1。若两支路电流都为零，仅凭电流无法确定电阻之比。
clips.text: 并联电路的分流规律。两个并联电阻两端的电压相同。两支路电流均不为零时，I₁/I₂＝R₂/R₁。若两支路电流都为零，仅凭电流无法确定电阻之比。

clips.send: 平面镜成像的大小。物体离平面镜更远时，像的实际大小仍与物体相等。由于观察距离变化，像看起来可能变小。
clips.text: 平面镜成像的大小。物体离平面镜更远时，像的实际大小仍与物体相等。由于观察距离变化，像看起来可能变小。

clips.send: 用电能表脉冲数求电能。电能表常数用 imp/kWh（脉冲数每千瓦时）或 r/kWh（转数每千瓦时）表示时，商的单位为 kWh。只数这段时间内的脉冲或完整转数。
clips.text: 用电能表脉冲数求电能。电能表常数用 imp/kWh（脉冲数每千瓦时）或 r/kWh（转数每千瓦时）表示时，商的单位为 kWh。只数这段时间内的脉冲或完整转数。

clips.send: 回声测距。回声时间包含沿同一路径的往返。用题目所给介质和条件下的声速。
clips.text: 回声测距。回声时间包含沿同一路径的往返。用题目所给介质和条件下的声速。

clips.send: 称重法测浮力。移项得 F浮等于G－T。让物体静止且不接触容器。在空气中测量重力时，此模型忽略空气浮力。
clips.text: 称重法测浮力。移项得 F浮＝G－T。让物体静止且不接触容器。在空气中测量重力时，此模型忽略空气浮力。

clips.send: 液体中的总压强。容器敞口时，液面处的压强是大气压；容器密闭时，取液面上方气体的压强。
clips.text: 液体中的总压强。容器敞口时，液面处的压强是大气压；容器密闭时，取液面上方气体的压强。

clips.send: 排水法测体积。末读数减初读数。物体完全浸没、没有液体溢出且不带气泡时，读数差等于物体总体积。
clips.text: 排水法测体积。末读数减初读数。物体完全浸没、没有液体溢出且不带气泡时，读数差等于物体总体积。

clips.send: 用电压求电阻功率。电压相同时，电阻越大，热功率越小。U 取该电阻两端的电压。
clips.text: 用电压求电阻功率。电压相同时，电阻越大，热功率越小。U 取该电阻两端的电压。

clips.send: 并联电路的电压。两条支路接在同一对节点之间。各支路两端的电压都等于并联部分两端的总电压。
clips.text: 并联电路的电压。两条支路接在同一对节点之间。各支路两端的电压都等于并联部分两端的总电压。

clips.send: 热机效率。对燃料热机，分母是燃料放出的热量。有用功和放热量必须对应同一时间段。
clips.text: 热机效率。对燃料热机，分母是燃料放出的热量。有用功和放热量必须对应同一时间段。

clips.send: 串联电路的电流。串联电路只有一条通路。各元件前后及元件之间的电流都相等。
clips.text: 串联电路的电流。串联电路只有一条通路。各元件前后及元件之间的电流都相等。

clips.send: 平均加速度。选定正方向，用末速度减去初速度，保留正负号。
clips.text: 平均加速度。选定正方向，用末速度减去初速度，保留正负号。

clips.send: 用电能表读数求电能。电能表末读数减初读数，得到这段时间消耗的电能。读数时留意小数位。
clips.text: 用电能表读数求电能。电能表末读数减初读数，得到这段时间消耗的电能。读数时留意小数位。

clips.send: 气体燃料按体积计算的放热量。热值用 J/ 立方米 表示时用此式。气体体积应与给出热值时的条件一致。
clips.text: 气体燃料按体积计算的放热量。热值用 J/m³ 表示时用此式。气体体积应与给出热值时的条件一致。

clips.send: 摄氏温度与热力学温度。温标读数换算才要加减 273.15。温差 1 ℃ 与温差 1 K 相等。
clips.text: 摄氏温度与热力学温度。温标读数换算才要加减 273.15。温差 1 ℃ 与温差 1 K 相等。

clips.send: 机械能。本式适用于只有动能和重力势能的情形。有弹簧储能时还要计入弹性势能。只有重力做功时，这里的机械能总和保持不变。
clips.text: 机械能。本式适用于只有动能和重力势能的情形。有弹簧储能时还要计入弹性势能。只有重力做功时，这里的机械能总和保持不变。

clips.send: 欧姆定律。I、U、R 应对应同一导体的同一工作状态。灯丝温度改变时，电阻会改变。
clips.text: 欧姆定律。I、U、R 应对应同一导体的同一工作状态。灯丝温度改变时，电阻会改变。

clips.send: 并联电路的总电阻。先把各支路电阻的倒数相加，再取倒数。两个有限正电阻并联时，总电阻比其中任一个都小。支路更多时继续加倒数。
clips.text: 并联电路的总电阻。先把各支路电阻的倒数相加，再取倒数。两个有限正电阻并联时，总电阻比其中任一个都小。支路更多时继续加倒数。

clips.send: 密度。质量和体积必须对应同一样品。1 g/ 立方厘米等于1 000 kg/ 立方米 。
clips.text: 密度。质量和体积必须对应同一样品。1 g/cm³＝1 000 kg/m³。

clips.send: 热平衡。两物体换热时，假设与容器及外界的热交换可忽略。两边均取热量的大小。
clips.text: 热平衡。两物体换热时，假设与容器及外界的热交换可忽略。两边均取热量的大小。

clips.send: 燃料按质量计算的放热量。本式求燃料完全燃烧放出的热量，被加热物体通常只吸收其中一部分。
clips.text: 燃料按质量计算的放热量。本式求燃料完全燃烧放出的热量，被加热物体通常只吸收其中一部分。

clips.send: 同样的路程，时间减半，速度会怎样变化？先在小实验中试一试，再用公式、单位和例题复习。
clips.text: 同样的路程，时间减半，速度会怎样变化？先在小实验中试一试，再用公式、单位和例题复习。

clips.send: 电功率。用电器两端的实际电压和通过它的实际电流。额定功率对应额定工作条件。平均电功率为 W/t。
clips.text: 电功率。用电器两端的实际电压和通过它的实际电流。额定功率对应额定工作条件。平均电功率为 W/t。

clips.send: 总功、有用功与额外功。提升重物时，有用功为 Gh。总功用拉力乘以绳子自由端沿拉力方向移动的距离。
clips.text: 总功、有用功与额外功。提升重物时，有用功为 Gh。总功用拉力乘以绳子自由端沿拉力方向移动的距离。

clips.send: 重力势能。高度从选定的零势能面竖直量起。近地面取 g 不变，本计算器的高度取零或正值。
clips.text: 重力势能。高度从选定的零势能面竖直量起。近地面取 g 不变，本计算器的高度取零或正值。

clips.send: 计入动滑轮组自重时的拉力。此模型中，各竖直承重绳段的拉力大小相等。匀速提升时，拉力还需克服动滑轮组的重力。忽略绳重和摩擦。
clips.text: 计入动滑轮组自重时的拉力。此模型中，各竖直承重绳段的拉力大小相等。匀速提升时，拉力还需克服动滑轮组的重力。忽略绳重和摩擦。

clips.send: 理想滑轮组的拉力。数承担动滑轮组和重物的绳段。各绳段竖直，重物匀速提升，忽略摩擦、绳重和动滑轮自重。
clips.text: 理想滑轮组的拉力。数承担动滑轮组和重物的绳段。各绳段竖直，重物匀速提升，忽略摩擦、绳重和动滑轮自重。

clips.send: 机械功。本式适用于恒力与物体运动同向的情形。托住静止的书时，支持力对书不做功。
clips.text: 机械功。本式适用于恒力与物体运动同向的情形。托住静止的书时，支持力对书不做功。

clips.send: 焦耳定律。电流要平方，电流和电阻应保持不变。纯电阻用电器消耗的电能全部转化为热；电动机还会输出机械能。
clips.text: 焦耳定律。电流要平方，电流和电阻应保持不变。纯电阻用电器消耗的电能全部转化为热；电动机还会输出机械能。

clips.send: 动能。先把速度平方。质量不变时，速度加倍，动能变为原来的四倍。
clips.text: 动能。先把速度平方。质量不变时，速度加倍，动能变为原来的四倍。

clips.send: 用功率求电能。用恒定功率或这段时间内的平均功率。kW 乘以 h 得到 kWh，它是电能单位。
clips.text: 用功率求电能。用恒定功率或这段时间内的平均功率。kW 乘以 h 得到 kWh，它是电能单位。

clips.send: 用力和速度求功率。取沿运动方向的力。求瞬时功率用瞬时速度；力恒定且与运动同向时，用平均速度可求平均功率。本计算器取沿运动方向的非负分力。
clips.text: 用力和速度求功率。取沿运动方向的力。求瞬时功率用瞬时速度；力恒定且与运动同向时，用平均速度可求平均功率。本计算器取沿运动方向的非负分力。

clips.send: 杠杆平衡条件。力臂是支点到力的作用线的垂直距离。两个力的转动效果方向相反。
clips.text: 杠杆平衡条件。力臂是支点到力的作用线的垂直距离。两个力的转动效果方向相反。

clips.send: 平均机械功率。功率表示做功的快慢。做同样多的功，时间越短，平均功率越大。
clips.text: 平均机械功率。功率表示做功的快慢。做同样多的功，时间越短，平均功率越大。

clips.send: 机械效率。有用功除以总功，通常用百分数表示。有用功不能大于总功。
clips.text: 机械效率。有用功除以总功，通常用百分数表示。有用功不能大于总功。

clips.send: 牛顿第二定律。先沿选定轴按正负号求合力。加速度的方向与合力方向相同。
clips.text: 牛顿第二定律。先沿选定轴按正负号求合力。加速度的方向与合力方向相同。

clips.send: 平均速度。用总路程除以总时间，停留时间也算在内。匀速运动时，这也是物体的速度。
clips.text: 平均速度。用总路程除以总时间，停留时间也算在内。匀速运动时，这也是物体的速度。

clips.send: 固体压强。取实际受力面积和垂直作用在受力面上的压力。1 平方厘米等于0.0001 平方米 。
clips.text: 固体压强。取实际受力面积和垂直作用在受力面上的压力。1 cm²＝0.0001 m²。

clips.send: 二力平衡。两个力必须作用在同一物体上，沿同一直线，方向相反。
clips.text: 二力平衡。两个力必须作用在同一物体上，沿同一直线，方向相反。
